# The Data Sync alarm asserts failing runs whichever axis actually breached

## Context

The Data Sync watchdog measures two independent axes — run status and committed-corpus age — and #15948 built them apart on purpose: a green pipeline can certify a growing content backlog forever, so run health cannot stand in for corpus health.

`buildAlarmBody` then throws that separation away in its last line. It closes every alarm with one hardcoded sentence:

```
The pipeline is degrading silently: runs fail on schedule and nothing else surfaces it.
```

It is emitted on every breach, whichever axis measured one.

## The Problem

The sentence is a claim about the run axis, printed without consulting it. When only the corpus axis breaches, the alarm asserts failing runs directly beneath its own contradicting measurement:

```
**Streak:** 0 consecutive failures on `dev`.
...
The pipeline is degrading silently: runs fail on schedule and nothing else surfaces it.
```

That is not hypothetical. It is how #17834 read for five days: streak 0, every scheduled run green, and the actual outage a dead corpus producer. #17920's diagnosis had to open by refuting the alarm's own prose — *"that line is template prose, and it is **wrong**"* — before it could describe the outage. A reader who trusts the sentence goes looking for a broken workflow that is in fact passing.

The blast radius is not one issue. Five archived alarm issues under `resources/content/issues/**` carry the same sentence over their own streaks (`issue-15962`, `issue-15972`, `issue-16428`, `issue-17131`, `issue-17322`), so the corpus the swarm greps for prior art teaches the wrong diagnosis too.

The title half of the same alarm already got this right: `buildAlarmTitle` names the corpus when the corpus axis breaches alone, and the spec arm pinning that behaviour has existed since #15948 (`buildAlarmTitle: corpus-only breach names the corpus, not a zero streak`). Title and body have simply disagreed about the same breach ever since.

## The Architectural Reality

- `buildScripts/dataSyncWatchdog.mjs` — `buildAlarmBody`, the fixed closing line. The function already receives everything needed to derive it: `consecutiveFailures`, and `corpusFacets` with a per-facet `stale` flag.
- `evaluateBreach` (same file) already records per-axis breach reasons, and the body already renders them under **Breach reasons**. The defect is confined to the closing sentence, which asserts rather than reads.
- `buildAlarmTitle` (same file) is the working precedent for axis-derived prose.
- The reasons array must not be the input: matching `reasons` prose to classify an axis is a containment check standing in for a measurement, and it breaks the moment a reason is reworded.

## The Fix

Derive the closing line from the axes that actually fired, read from the structured inputs:

- run axis fired ⟺ `consecutiveFailures > 0`;
- corpus axis fired ⟺ any facet carries `stale: true`, and the line names those facets rather than counting them;
- both, either, or neither compose without a special case; the no-axis fallback keeps a truthful generic sentence for the forced-dispatch dry run.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] With a zero streak and a stale facet, the body contains no assertion that runs are failing — the negative arm names the shipped sentence literally, so it fails against the current source rather than passing on a wording mismatch.
- [ ] With a non-zero streak and every facet fresh, the body makes no claim about the corpus.
- [ ] With both axes breached, both survive into the body; neither stands in for the pair.
- [ ] A stale-facet line names the stale facets only, never a fresh sibling.
- [ ] The axis classification reads `consecutiveFailures` and each facet's `stale` flag, never the `reasons` prose.
- [ ] `buildAlarmTitle`'s existing corpus-only arm stays green — the pair must agree, not swap which half is wrong.

## Out of Scope

- The corpus outage itself. The producer was ruled NOT_PLANNED on the Brain side (`neomjs/neo-agent-brain#289`, `#291`, 2026-08-31) and the successor lane is #17416. This ticket makes the alarm describe the outage honestly; it does not end it.
- The watchdog's thresholds, axis definitions, and two-axis design. #17920 already ruled the corpus axis correct — it is the only thing that noticed.
- The five archived alarm bodies. They are historical records of what the alarm said, and rewriting them would destroy the evidence that it said it.

## Avoided Traps

- **Deleting the sentence.** The closing line is the only plain-language statement of what breached; a body that ends on a reasons table reads as a stack trace. The fix is to make it true, not to remove it.
- **Classifying axes by matching `reasons` strings.** Wording coincidence standing in for a measurement — the same species the alarm already suffers from.
- **Treating this as a #17920 leftover to bundle later.** The alarm is the live carrier for an outage that is currently unowned; a misleading body costs a reader per breach episode, and the episode is open now.

## Related

- #17920 — the diagnosis that had to refute this line first; AC-5 there names it. Its Engine-side ACs landed in #17927; its producer-dependent ACs belong to #17416.
- #17834 — the standing alarm that carried the false sentence for five days, currently open at 18+ consecutive failures.
- #15948 / #15956 — the two-axis watchdog design, and `buildAlarmTitle`'s axis-aware precedent.
- `neomjs/neo-agent-brain#289` / `#291` — the producer disposition (NOT_PLANNED, superseded to #17416).
